0.content:
Kusayla led Dakan Al-Ahmar, an Eremite brigade under the larger Deshret's Relics. He raised Dehya among his mercenaries. He was a slapdash, boastful man who put on plays and told hero stories for her, including the Legend of the Lion. Dehya came to see him as a criminal and left after a final argument. In Lionsblood (3.5) she learned that Deshret's Relics bound members with blackmail "records". Kusayla never let her be "recorded", lied and took beatings to protect her, and arranged her place with the Blazing Beasts and her job with the Homayanis. Years ago he went back to the Relics' headquarters and burned the records, dying in the fire and freeing his men.

His cane, which he needed after the beatings, hid the toy sword from their childhood plays; Dehya inherited it. In a letter found in a bottle he wrote that he found her as a baby alone in the sands, told his men she was his child by a woman, and was never her father. He said she had a freedom and kindness he could only dream of, and that how she lived was up to her. Dehya resolved to find her birth parents to tell them who raised her.

1.comment: Dehya: Dunyarzad and the Homayani family
1.content:
Dunyarzad Homayani, daughter of the merchant Shahzaman, was dying of Eleazar when Dehya was hired to guard her. Dehya caught her sneaking out to revive the Sabzeruz Festival. Respecting her determination, she let Dunyarzad "hire" her at half her father's rate to cover for her. She secretly sold her own claymore and donated the Mora to the festival, which is why she was still learning a new greatsword when kidnappers struck. After the sages fell and Eleazar was cured, Dehya quit as she had always planned, but they remain close. Dunyarzad throws her birthday parties and takes her dancing.

Lionsblood showed that the job was Kusayla's doing. Kusayla had once saved baby Dunyarzad and her father from bandits. Years later he asked Shahzaman to hire his daughter and secretly paid part of her fee. Shahzaman had also supplied Dakan Al-Ahmar with food and medicine (not weapons) and was taken into custody afterwards. In 6.6 Dehya found Dunyarzad praying the night before the battle and told her she had always been strong and ambitious.

2.content:
The Blazing Beasts are the Eremite band Dehya joined after leaving her father's brigade, and her chosen family. Kusayla secretly arranged for them to take her in so she could leave Dakan Al-Ahmar without harassment. They gave her the title Flame-Mane and sing campfire songs about "our precious Dehya". She is their most famous member but says she is not the boss, though their problems always end up on her plate. Her Vision helped her bring more fighters into the band.

During the limited-time Whirling Waltz event (5.6), some of the Blazing Beasts starred in a Fontainian adventure film, and the Traveler and Paimon agreed to become the band's official partners for far-flung commissions.

3.content: Candace, the Guardian of Aaru Village, is one of Dehya's dearest friends. Dehya calls the village a safe haven. Her Eremites behave there when she brings them, which Candace appreciates, and Candace says Dehya looks like trouble but is "really quite adorable". Dehya keeps pushing her to rest, shop and wear the jewellery she gives her, with little success. During a limited-time 5.3 event she got Candace to come to Lantern Rite in Liyue, though only after the villagers insisted. The two often travel together on business.

4.content: In 3.0 the sages trapped Sumeru City in a repeating Sabzeruz Festival through the Akasha. Each loop, Dehya fought off mercenaries trying to kidnap Dunyarzad. The Traveler convinced her of the loop by knowing her secret about the sold greatsword. Though she could not see Nahida or the real Dunyarzad's spirit, she sensed Dunyarzad's aura. She then reasoned that the sages were using the Akasha to extract and pool people's minds into "a single, massive brain". Her own training dummy helped prove the city was a dream.

5.content: In Aaru Village (3.1), Dehya broke up a fight between Cyno and Alhaitham. She guided the Traveler to Caravan Ribat to trap the radicals behind the missing Village Keepers, explaining on the way how the Wall of Samiel shuts the Eremites out. She persuaded Rahman's band to help. In 3.2 she and the Traveler won Tighnari's help and tracked Dottore to Port Ormos, where they realised he had sent them the wrong way. They rushed back to save Haypasia at Pardis Dhyai. On Jnagarbha Day she led the Eremites in drawing the guards off with Isak disguised as Kusanali, then freed the Traveler from confinement. At the feast she cheered the sages' downfall and teased Alhaitham and Cyno.

6.comment: Dehya: Rahman and the right arm
6.content: Rahman's Eremites had kidnapped Aaru's Village Keepers, believing it would revive King Deshret. Dehya tried to win them over, and when Rahman would not trust Alhaitham's word she offered her right arm as payment for her friends' honesty. He ordered it cut off, then stopped, saying it would be like cutting off his own fingers. When he returned only one hostage the next day, she charged and beat him. After the group found Kasala's record of King Deshret's sacrifice, Rahman joined their cause.

7.content: Alhaitham planned the Jnagarbha Day operation with Dehya. Afterwards he offered her a position at the Akademiya, saying it was a waste for someone so capable to remain among the Eremites. She refused, joking that she would not last ten seconds and that a predictable life is not for her. She mocks his "long, convoluted sentences" in a "snooty tone"; he understands, and sighs.

8.content: Dehya rates Cyno highly because he does not suffer fools. During a limited-time 3.5 event she stood in for him at the Akademiya while he was abroad. In 4.6 she and Candace found him at Caravan Ribat asking about a lone old man heading into the desert; afterwards she muttered that he was lucky the others caught up, and wondered what he was thinking "trying to play the lone hero". Tighnari almost hired her as a desert guide before cancelling, which she suspects was because of the heat. In 3.2 she recruited him, told him to rest after a lightning strike and called him one of those who always think they can push through pain.

9.content: At the start of the Fontaine chapter (4.0), Dehya, back from escorting goods, met the Traveler and Paimon at Caravan Ribat as they prepared to leave Sumeru. She offered to raise a mercenary escort to the border, and when they declined she observed that true heroes always seem to leave quietly. She said that whether as client or friend, they were always welcome to come find her.

key: Truth Amongst the Pages of Purana
10.content:
When Irminsul's malfunction threatened Sumeru, Nahida and the new sages evacuated the rainforest. Dehya's Eremites escorted the civilians west to Aaru Village, with Candace receiving them. Naphis put Dehya, Candace and Nefer in charge of negotiating between the groups. On the eve of battle she wished for a stiff drink, received free perfume from Dori (thanks for a caravan she and Candace had rescued) and encouraged a praying Dunyarzad. During the operation she, Cyno, Candace, Jeht, Rahman and Rana stormed Sumeru City as a diversion and faced Pantalone's decoy. Afterwards she made sure everyone on the evacuation list got home and parted from Sethos at Caravan Ribat.

In 6.6 she was one of three trial characters with Cyno and Candace for part of the assault. Parting from Sethos at Caravan Ribat, she remarked that only desert folk know how far their faith has faded, though they still speak of the gods as part of their lives.

11.content: Meeting Nefer of Nod-Krai at the Temple of Silence, Dehya asked whether she was from the desert and then asked plainly what lay behind her interest in it. Nefer invited her into the Curatorium's network. Dehya, who values intelligence in the desert, accepted after laying the cards on the table and said she looked forward to a fruitful partnership with someone so no-nonsense. Nefer had long heard of the "kind-hearted Flame-Mane", her spending on raising a child, and the rumour that her gauntlet's power ties to King Deshret.

12.content: The image carved on Dehya's arm armour is Shesepankh, one of the desert's Seven Pillars. Before the 6.6 assault, Bennu spoke through Candace's shield. Dehya asked if her gauntlet could talk too; Shesepankh answered that it was its own image carved there and lent her its strength. Sethos later invited her and Candace to the Temple of Silence to meet the Pillars whose symbols they wear. The origin of the gauntlet is not explained.

13.content: Sethos once shared water with her mercenaries in the desert; she calls him a nice, down-to-earth guy, and he names her the second-best desert guide after himself. Dori hires her for caravans as the best value. Dehya hopes Dori can source the supplies mercs cannot get elsewhere, and in 6.6 Dori gave her perfume free of charge. Nilou offered her face powder after the sages fell, which Dehya passed to Candace; in 5.7 Dehya recorded Fontaine's clockwork dancers so Nilou and Dunyarzad could use the moves.

14.content: During the limited-time Whirling Waltz event (5.6), Dehya and some of the Blazing Beasts were guests at Fontaine's Chevalmarin Film Fantasyland after starring in an adventure film. She was dropped from the cast for wrecking half a set in an action scene. Uncle Scimitar became a minor star when the lead improvised shooting him instead of fighting. Over drinks at The Rusty Rudder she ordered confidently, said a stable job gets boring, and signed the Traveler and Paimon up as partners of the Blazing Beasts.

15.content: In two 5.7 anecdotes Dehya is in Fontaine as bodyguard for a merchant ship. She films the clockwork dancer Coppelius for Dunyarzad and Nilou and worries who could manage the lifts, deciding she will grit her teeth and lead. At Chiori's boutique, Chiori sees how her eyes linger on dancewear, makes her flip a coin to find out what she really wants, and Dehya laughs and orders a dress for herself.

16.content: Limited-time appearances, canon but not universally known. In Windblume's Breath (3.5) she stood in for Cyno at the Akademiya's door. At the Akademiya Extravaganza (3.6) she shopped with Candace and Faruzan and spotted kidnap-for-hire mercenaries disguised as tourists. In Summertide Scales and Tales (4.8) she had turned down a suspicious commission to find a certain book. In Chromatic Ode of Candies and Roses (5.1) she proposed the new Sabzeruz carriage parade with Dunyarzad. At Lantern Rite in Springtime Charms (5.3) she made a gift envelope for Candace in Liyue.

17.content:
Her yearly birthday letters to the Traveler (each with her Goldflame Tajine):
- 2023: a party at Aaru Village with Dunyarzad, Candace and Setaria, and a confiscated bag of rice Candace meant for pillow-fight "oomph".
- 2024: Dunyarzad organised her party; she could not choose among dresses and wished it were as easy as picking a weapon.
- 2025: a Natlanese client's tales of the Traveler, and snacks shared with the kids she supports.
- 2026: a big contract and new light weapons that felt wrong, so she is considering dual claymores.
